meta.name: Númenor
meta.sub: The Land of Gift before the Downfall

peoples.title: Númenóreans
peoples.hint: the Dúnedain, the Edain of the Three Houses given the Land of Gift; mariners, shepherds, foresters and builders on every part of the isle

peoples.title: The Faithful (Elendili)
peoples.hint: the Elf-friends who kept faith with the Valar; strongest in the west under the Lords of Andúnië, later gathered about Rómenna in the east

peoples.title: The King's Men
peoples.hint: the party of the later kings who turned against the Valar and the Eldar; they ruled from Armenelos and in the end served Sauron's Temple

peoples.title: Guild of Venturers
peoples.hint: the sea-farers' guild that Aldarion founded; its ships sailed from Rómenna to Middle-earth (Unfinished Tales, Aldarion and Erendis)

peoples.title: Lords of Andúnië
peoples.hint: descendants of Silmariën through Valandil, chief of the Faithful; seated at Andúnië in the Andustar until Ar-Gimilzôr moved them to Rómenna; Amandil and Elendil

peoples.title: Eagles of Manwë
peoples.hint: the Witnesses of Manwë, who came to the summit of the Meneltarma in the days of the Three Prayers; eagles also nested about the Forostar and Sorontil

peoples.title: Shepherds of the Mittalmar
peoples.hint: the sheep-farming folk of the Inlands, as at Emerië and the lands of Hallatan of Hyarastorni (Aldarion and Erendis)

battles.title: The Downfall of Númenor
battles.hint: when Ar-Pharazôn set foot on Aman, Eru changed the world; the Meneltarma broke out in fire and the whole land sank under a great wave; Tar-Míriel perished seeking the Hallow. Akallabêth; Appendix A

battles.title: Burning of Nimloth and the fires of the Temple
battles.hint: on Sauron's counsel Ar-Pharazôn cut down the White Tree; its wood was the first fire on the altar of the great Temple, and men were burned there in sacrifice to Melkor. Akallabêth

battles.title: Isildur takes the fruit of Nimloth
battles.date: shortly before the felling of Nimloth
battles.hint: Isildur went in disguise into the guarded court of the King, took a fruit of the White Tree and fought his way out, sorely wounded. Akallabêth

battles.title: Persecution of the Faithful
battles.hint: the Faithful, who dwelt mostly about Rómenna, were accused of treason against the King, spied on and taken to be slain or burned in the Temple at Armenelos. Akallabêth

journeys.title: The coming of the Edain to Elenna
journeys.travellers: Elros and the Edain of the Three Houses
journeys.hint: the Edain sailed out of the east over the sea, guided by the Star of Eärendil, to the land the Valar raised for them; the landing place is not named in the books

stages.title: Out of the east
stages.hint: many ships of the Edain sail west over the Great Sea following the Star of Eärendil

stages.title: The Meneltarma rises from the sea
stages.hint: approx: the mariners see the land of Elenna and its tall mountain far off

stages.title: Into the bay
stages.hint: approx: the fleet comes in among the eastern promontories; the books do not name the landing

stages.title: Landing in the east
stages.hint: approx: landing at the head of the firth where Rómenna later stood

stages.title: Armenelos founded
stages.hint: Elros Tar-Minyatur, first King, builds the City of the Kings in Arandor

stages.title: The holy mountain
stages.hint: the Meneltarma in the midst of the land, whose summit was hallowed to Eru

journeys.title: The road of the Three Prayers
journeys.travellers: the King of Númenor and a great multitude of the people
journeys.dates: each year in spring, midsummer and autumn, from the early kings until the prayers were neglected and at last forbidden
journeys.hint: at the Erukyermë, the Erulaitalë and the Eruhantalë the King went up the Meneltarma to the Hallow of Eru, and the people followed in silence (Unfinished Tales; Akallabêth)

stages.title: From the City of the Kings
stages.hint: the King sets out from Armenelos

stages.title: Westward on the road
stages.hint: approx: along the paved highway toward the mountain

stages.title: Noirinan
stages.hint: the procession enters the Valley of the Tombs between the southern roots of the Pillar

stages.title: Past the Tombs of the Kings
stages.hint: the tombs of the kings and queens at the head of the valley

stages.title: The winding ascent
stages.hint: the path climbs spirally up the mountain

stages.title: The Hallow of Eru
stages.hint: on the open summit, without roof or altar, the King speaks the prayer; no other voice is heard there

journeys.title: Aldarion and Erendis
journeys.travellers: Tar-Aldarion the Mariner, Erendis, and their daughter Ancalimë
journeys.hint: the tale of the mariner prince, the haven of Rómenna, the court at Armenelos and the white house in Emerië (Unfinished Tales, Aldarion and Erendis)

stages.title: Rómenna, haven of the Venturers
stages.hint: Aldarion, Lord of the Ships and Havens, sails from Rómenna to Middle-earth

stages.title: The Calmindon
stages.hint: Aldarion raises the light-tower on Tol Uinen in the bay

stages.title: Betrothal and wedding in Armenelos
stages.hint: Erendis comes to the court of Tar-Meneldur; she is betrothed to Aldarion and at last they are wed

stages.title: The white house in Emerië
stages.hint: Aldarion builds a white house for Erendis among the sheep-lands; after his long absences she withdraws there with Ancalimë

stages.title: The mariner returns
stages.hint: Aldarion comes home over the sea and finds his wife gone from Armenelos

stages.title: The shut door
stages.hint: he rides to Emerië and is turned away from the house; their estrangement is never healed

stages.title: Ancalimë at Hyarastorni
stages.hint: approx: grown weary of her mother's house, Ancalimë goes to the household of Hallatan of Hyarastorni

journeys.title: The last days of Númenor
journeys.travellers: Ar-Pharazôn's Great Armament; Elendil, Isildur and Anárion with the Faithful
journeys.hint: the King's fleet sails into the West against the Ban of the Valar while the Faithful wait in their ships off the east coast and escape the Downfall (Akallabêth; Appendix A)

stages.title: The Armament is prepared
stages.hint: Ar-Pharazôn, counselled by Sauron, builds the greatest fleet ever seen

stages.title: The fleets gather in the west
stages.hint: approx: the fleets darken the sea upon the west of the land; no haven is named

stages.title: Into the West
stages.hint: the Armament sails west toward Aman; the King sets foot on the shore of Aman

stages.title: The Faithful at Rómenna
stages.hint: Elendil and his sons gather the Faithful, the seedling of Nimloth and the seven Seeing-stones, as Amandil bade before he sailed west alone

stages.title: Nine ships off the east coast
stages.hint: the ships of Elendil lie off the coast and take no part in the King's war

stages.title: The Downfall
stages.hint: the Meneltarma breaks out in fire and the land is swallowed by the sea

stages.title: Driven east
stages.hint: a great wind drives Elendil's nine ships east toward Middle-earth

art.subject: A tall lone mountain rising from green rolling uplands, five long low ridges running out from its foot, a thin path winding up to a flat grassy summit under a clear morning sky.
A white city of towers and courts on a hill in open pasture-land, a slender white tree in a walled court, seen in the gold light of late afternoon.
A busy harbour town at the head of a long narrow sea-inlet, tall-masted ships at stone quays and green hills behind, at sunrise.
A haven town climbing the steep slopes above a western bay, a tower on a nearby hill, the sea glowing at sunset.
A green haven where a quiet river meets a wide bay, framed by evergreen fragrant trees in flower, a white ship with a swan prow at anchor, in soft morning light.
A narrow valley between two long ridges at the foot of a great mountain, with tombs cut into the rock at its head, in still grey dawn light.
A small rocky isle in a bay with a tall slender light-tower, its beacon lit against the evening sky over calm water.
Tall mariners and shepherds in plain cloaks on a grassy shore beside a great ship, the mountain far off behind them, on a bright windy day.
A small company of cloaked people loading a white sapling and covered chests onto ships at night in a quiet harbour, lanterns shaded.
A mountain breaking out in fire as a vast green wave rises over a white city and the land tilts into the sea, under a black storm sky.
A huge domed temple on a hill in a city at dusk, dark smoke pouring from the opening in its silver roof.
A walled moonlit court with a single white tree bearing pale fruit, guards with torches running across the flagstones at night.

notes: Promontory bearings are set 72 degrees apart (Forostar due north); the text gives only their names and the five-pointed shape, so exact bearings are judgment.
Sizes follow the Description: Mittalmar about 250 miles (about 380 to 400 km here) across; promontories 160 km wide and about 340 km long from the edge of the Mittalmar.
Meneltarma placed a little west of the exact middle of the Mittalmar ('near its centre'); Armenelos about 85 km east of it and Rómenna about 40 km beyond: the distances are not given.
Andúnië set in a bay cut into the western end of the Andustar; the texts say only that it lay on a bay of the west coast, with Oromet nearby. Its bay is drawn on the northern part of the end.
Ondosto placed in the south of the Forostar on the road between the Valley of the Tombs and Andúnië; the course of the road between named points is a guess.
Tower of Tar-Meneldur, House of the Lords of Andúnië, White House of Erendis and Hyarastorni are placed by judgment near the places the texts tie them to.

Several features carry descriptive names (Highlands of the Forostar, Highlands of the Andustar, Hills of Orrostar, Cliffs of Hyarnustar, Fir-woods of the Andustar, Forests of Hyarrostar, Vineyards, Grain-lands, Pastures, Marshes of the Siril, Northern bays of the Andustar): the texts describe them but give no proper name.
The first landing of the Edain is not located in the books; the journey brings them in from the east (they followed the Star from Middle-earth) to the Bay of Rómenna as a guess.
The fleets of the Great Armament are said to have darkened the sea 'upon the west of the land'; no haven is named, and the stage near Andúnië is a guess.
Persecution of the Faithful is anchored at Rómenna, where the Faithful dwelt; the burnings themselves were in the Temple at Armenelos.
Moriondë (an eastern haven) appears only in The Lost Road (History of Middle-earth) and is left off the map.
The Siril is given its source in Noirinan and its mouth in the southern bay between Hyarnustar and Hyarrostar, as the Description says it ran south; Nindamos is on the east side of its mouth.
